exposure: Mode of delivery (successful vaginal delivery after cesarean section vs. failed vaginal delivery after cesarean section)
outcome: Success of vaginal delivery after cesarean section (VBAC)
cohort: The study included 738 pregnant women who previously underwent a cesarean section and were attempting a second delivery, selected from a hospital between September 2018 and August 2020.
finding: Fetal abdominal circumference, fetal head orientation, Bishop score, and epidural anesthesia during labor were identified as independent factors affecting the success of VBAC, with successful VBAC deliveries showing significantly lower postpartum hemorrhage compared to failed VBAC deliveries, while other maternal and infant outcomes were similar.
mod_finding: The amount of postpartum hemorrhage was significantly lower in pregnant women who had a successful vaginal delivery after cesarean section compared to those who failed vaginal delivery.
